ADR-001 — outlet_staff sebagai identitas kanonik orang di outlet
nodes.rationale: Decision: define single canonical entity outlet_staff (roles crew/kasir/spv/kepala_outlet) as source of truth for outlet people identity; all outlet actions (absen, transaksi, stok, terima kiriman) attributed to outlet_staff; new POS will link to outlet_staff rather than creating its own person table. Alternatives rejected: (1) reuse old pos_cashiers — rejected because new POS doesn't exist yet and attendance covers a broader set of people than just cashiers; (2) separate accounts per system — rejected because person data would fragment across 3+ systems, making owner dashboard attribution inaccurate and sync expensive. Consequences: (+) consistent per-person attribution across modules, accurate owner dashboard, new POS just references outlet_staff; (-) requires migration/mapping when new POS is uploaded (mapping cashiers to outlet_staff).

nodes.label: ADR-002 — Supabase sebagai reporting hub untuk Owner Dashboard
nodes.rationale: Decision: make Supabase the single reporting hub; heavy aggregation via materialized views + pg_cron with layered refresh (today ~2min, historical hourly/daily); sync outlets + sales aggregates from Ecosystem via Edge Function + pg_cron (amended by ADR-004/ADR-006 since new modules live in a separate Supabase project); compliance (MySQL) becomes a secondary widget deferred to later phase; central HR (Postgres) not integrated; dashboard is a single Next.js app reading Supabase. Alternative rejected: live cross-DB query joining Supabase+Postgres+MySQL at runtime — rejected as fragile to source schema changes, slow at high transaction volume, expensive, and tightens coupling between systems. Consequences: (+) fast dashboard (<1s, pre-aggregated), cheap, isolated from source changes; (+) near-real-time is sufficient for owner decisions; (-) data latency of minutes/hours accepted since owner needs analytics not a live ticker; (-) requires cross-account sync (Edge Function + pg_cron) for outlets & sales.

nodes.label: ADR-003 — Face matching client-side (face-api.js) + GPS/selfie
nodes.rationale: Decision: use 1:1 client-side face matching with face-api.js on outlet device (descriptor vector, calibratable euclidean threshold ~<0.5); enrollment done by SPV/Kepala Outlet (1-3 photos); layered MVP anti-fraud = GPS radius + selfie audit + server timestamp; descriptor cached locally for offline tolerance (attendance queues, syncs when online); active liveness (blink/gesture) deferred to a later phase. Alternatives rejected: (1) server-side ML pipeline (1:N embedding + liveness) — rejected as requiring large infra/effort, overkill for a small team's anti-proxy-attendance need; (2) GPS+selfie only without face matching — rejected because it technically does not prevent proxy attendance (titip-absen). Consequences: (+) no ML server needed, lightweight, runs in outlet device browser, offline-tolerant; (+) layered (face + GPS + selfie audit) sufficient for MVP; (-) without liveness, vulnerable to photo-of-photo spoofing, mitigated by live camera + GPS + selfie audit for SPV spot-checks, liveness to follow; (-) accuracy depends on outlet camera quality/lighting, requiring threshold calibration.
